source: (1) Faros, 'AI Engineering Report 2026: The Acceleration Whiplash' (PDF, 'This version of the report reflects analysis as of March 2026'; landing page labels it 'AI ENGINEERING REPORT Q2 2026'). Opened landing page https://www.faros.ai/research/ai-acceleration-whiplash and the full PDF https://pages.faros.ai/hubfs/AI_Engineering_Report_2026_The_Acceleration_Whiplash_Faros.pdf . No named individual authors. (2) Ron Powell and Jacob Schmitt, '5 key takeaways from the 2026 State of Software Delivery', CircleCI blog, Feb 18, 2026. Opened: https://circleci.com/blog/five-takeaways-2026-software-delivery-report/ . Full report 'The 2026 State of Software Delivery' (CircleCI, sponsored by Thoughtworks per the blog; authors Ron Powell, Jacob Schmitt). Opened: https://circleci.com/landing-pages/assets/2026-state-of-software-delivery-report.pdf . (3) Critique: Rob Bowley, 'More code, less delivery but does the CircleCI 2026 Report really show 1 in 20 teams are benefiting?', blog.robbowley.net, April 2, 2026. Opened: https://blog.robbowley.net/2026/04/02/more-code-less-delivery-but-does-the-circleci-2026-report-really-show-1-in-20-teams-are-benefiting/
data_type: Telemetry from both vendors, observational and correlational. Faros: within-team comparison of low vs high AI adoption quarters. CircleCI: CI/CD pipeline run data, year-on-year comparison; no direct measure of AI use.
sample_and_method: Faros: 'two years of data from 22,000 developers and 4,000 teams across the Faros platform' (customers; 'Organizations running on non-standard infrastructure were excluded'). Telemetry 'aggregated from task management systems, IDEs, static code analysis tools, CI/CD pipelines, version control systems, incident management systems, and HR system metadata.' Method: metrics standardised per company; Spearman's rank correlation with AI usage; only metrics 'with data from at least 6 companies and statistically significant correlations (p-value < 0.05)'; for each team, percent change between 'the two quarters of lowest AI adoption and the two quarters of highest AI adoption'; focus on teams moving above the 50% weekly-active-user threshold. Deployment frequency and lead time come from only about 10% of the dataset. The 2025 comparison is to a different cross-section ('not a longitudinal panel'; prior dataset 'more than 10,000 developers and 1,255 teams'). CircleCI: '28,738,317 workflows', every day September 1 to 28, 2025, CircleCI projects with more than one contributor and workflows that ran at least 5 times; compared with the prior year's equivalent data; industry data from Clearbit. Teams are banded by throughput percentile (bottom 25%, median, top 25/10/5%).
vendor_interest: Yes, both. Faros sells an engineering-intelligence platform for AI spend, productivity and governance ('Track token spend, outcomes, and AI engineering efficiency'); the report closes recommending an 'AI harness' and 'context engine' and says deeper churn analysis 'is available to individual organizations ... using Faros.' CircleCI sells CI/CD and closes by pitching its 'autonomous validation' product as the fix for the bottleneck it describes. Each vendor's data points to the stage of the pipeline it sells into.
headline_figures: Faros PDF: 'Task completion is up 34%. Epics completed per developer are up 66%. Tasks involving code specifically have increased 210%.' / 'Bugs per developer are up 54%. The incidents-to-PR ratio has more than tripled. Median review time has increased 5X. 31% more PRs are merging without any review.' Throughput table (low to high AI adoption): '+33.7% task throughput per developer', '+66.2% epics completed per developer', '+16.2% PR merge rate per developer', '+210% tasks completed per team with an associated PR', '-11% deployments per week (measured by 10% of the dataset)', '+861% code churn (lines deleted to lines added per quarter, for merged code)'. Text: 'deployments per week are down 11.7%. More code is being written and merged, but it is not being released to production as frequently.' / 'For the organizations that instrument this, lead time has increased 480.4%... the specific figure should be treated directionally.' Quality: '+242.7% incidents per PR', '+57.9% monthly incidents', '+54% bugs per developer, up from +9% in our prior report', '+28.7% bugs per PR', '+12.6% percentage of reopened Jira tickets'. Complexity: '+51.3% average PR size'. Flow: '+225.2% average time a task spends in progress', '+441.5 median time in PR review' (percent). Adoption: '60% acceptance rate of AI-generated code (up from 20% in prior dataset)'. CircleCI blog: 'the average number of daily workflow runs increased 59% year over year'; 'The top 5% of teams nearly doubled their throughput, increasing daily workflow runs by 97%. The median team? Up just 4%, while the bottom quartile saw no measurable increase at all.'; 'For the median team, feature branch throughput increased 15%, but on the main branch, throughput fell by 7%.'; 'Main branch success rates dropped to 70.8%, the lowest in over five years'; '72 minutes to get back to green for the typical team, up 13% from last year.'; top 5%: 'main branch throughput increased 26% while feature branch activity grew 85%'; 'they represent fewer than 1 in 20 teams.' CircleCI PDF charts: median team all branches 4.3%, feature 15.2%, main -6.8%; p90 all 47.2%, feature 49.3%, main 1.0%; p95 all 96.8%, feature 85.1%, main 26.2%.
metric_layer: Faros covers input/usage (adoption, acceptance rate), activity/output (tasks, epics, PRs merged, PR size, churn), delivery (deployments per week, lead time, both from about 10% of teams), and quality (bugs, incidents, reopened tickets, unreviewed merges). CircleCI covers activity (workflow runs on all and feature branches), a delivery proxy (main-branch workflow runs, which are not deployments) and pipeline quality (main-branch success rate, time to recover). Neither measures financial outcomes; CircleCI's '250 additional hours' and '12 full-time engineers' are illustrative calculations, not observed costs.
respondent_role_split: Not applicable: telemetry, no respondents. Faros reports no role split, though it argues review load falls on senior engineers ('the tax falling on senior engineers'). This is interpretation, not a measured split. CircleCI splits by throughput band, company size, team size, industry and region, not by role.
workload_signal: Faros: '+67.4% daily PR contexts per developer', '+17.7% daily task contexts per developer', '+13.8% work restarts per developer', '+26% in-progress tasks with no PR or activity in the past 7 days'; median time to first PR review +156.6%, average time in PR review +199.6%. Faros says reviewers 'appear to be working harder to bring that code up to a standard it should have met before the PR was opened.' No hours, burnout or pressure measures. CircleCI: recovery time 72 minutes, up 13%; feature-branch MTTR up 25%, 'from 64 minutes in 2024 to nearly 80 minutes in 2025'. Its hours lost and 'higher burnout' are asserted or modelled, not measured.
definition_of_value_offered: Partly, in both cases. Faros treats epics completed as 'the single finding most directly tied to business outcomes' and says 'Throughput measures what was shipped, not what survived. Code churn is the asterisk on every output number in this section.' Its recommendations ask leaders to track incident-to-PR ratio, monthly incidents normalised to lines changed, PR size, work restarts and churn, net of quality. CircleCI defines success as shipped changes, not code written: 'success in the AI era isn't determined by how fast code gets written. It's determined by how fast it can be validated, integrated, and recovered.' It uses main-branch throughput as the delivery measure. Bowley sharpens this: 'Throughput should be an end-to-end metric... The only meaningful "throughput" measure is against the main branch.' None defines a financial return or a threshold for 'paying off'.
removal_counterfactual: None directly. Faros compares each team's lowest and highest AI-adoption quarters, which is a within-team before/after on adoption, not tool removal. CircleCI compares year on year with no AI/no-AI split.
key_quotes: 1. 'Throughput measures what was shipped, not what survived.' (Faros, The Acceleration Whiplash, 2026). 2. 'Writing code is no longer the constraint. Review, validation, integration, recovery.' (CircleCI blog, Feb 18, 2026).
caveats: Both are vendor telemetry, observational and correlational; neither isolates AI as the cause. Faros says 'Correlation, not coincidence' on its landing page, but its method is correlational (Spearman, p<0.05), and it admits churn 'cannot resolve the ambiguity' (rework vs productive refactoring). Faros's 2026 data does not show flat delivery overall: epics per developer rose 66.2% and PR merges 16.2%, while deployments fell 11.7% and lead time rose 480.4%, both from only about 10% of teams and with 'High variance'. The 'activity up, delivery flat' framing fits CircleCI (median main branch -6.8%) better than Faros. Faros landing-page figures are rounded or differ from the PDF ('+28% Bugs per PR' vs 28.7%; '10X Code Churn' vs +861%, which the PDF calls '9.6 times'). Its comparisons with the 2025 report are 'directional' because the samples differ. CircleCI never measures AI use. Its blog heading 'AI-generated code breaks more often' attributes pipeline failures to AI without evidence in the data. CircleCI's blog says top-10% main-branch throughput 'increased only 1%'; the PDF says 'essentially flat' (1.0%). Bowley's critique: CI pipeline runs are 'not production deployments, it is not features shipped'; the top 5% have an odd average pipeline duration of '6 seconds' (he suggests 'an error in the report'). The PDF summary table (p.24) does show Top 5% duration '6s', and also top-5% mean time to recovery '1m 36s', against an average of '26h 32m 21s'; one team running about 130,000 workflows a day (the PDF shows #1 at 135,888) could skew aggregates. Bowley also writes 'Average teams are up 4%' where CircleCI says median, and 'top 10% ... aggregated throughput up nearly 50%' where the PDF shows 47.2% all-branch and 49.3% feature-branch. The CircleCI figures are a single 28-day window compared with a prior year.
access: Opened in full: Faros landing page and PDF; CircleCI blog and 27-page report PDF (text extracted with pdftotext; the p.24 summary table is an image and was read by rendering the page, confirming Top 5% duration '6s'); Bowley's post. Not verified: the Thoughtworks sponsorship rests on the CircleCI blog only; Faros appendix charts are images and were not read; the Faros 2025 report (source of earlier 'delivery flat' claims) was not opened in this task.
